--1 - Containment of Contaminated Area(s)

Containment of the basement with polyethylene drop sheets and zipper door(s), using negative air pressure (If permitted by actual conditions at the property), or an equivalent method, in order to prevent the cross contamination of mold spores, dust/debris and other particulates to other areas of the property.

- All personal belongings to be removed.

-- Topical & Abrasive Mold Treatment

-Topical Treatment Process:
Removal of mold from the areas by means of manual wirebrushing, or other topical and abrasive removal techniques. This is done in conjunction with HEPA vacuuming, and the application of an advanced, two-stage mold remediation protocol, initiating with high-precision stain removal techniques to revitalize the aesthetics of affected surfaces. This is seamlessly followed by the strategic application of our proprietary fungicides, meticulously designed to eliminate mold spores, thereby ensuring your space is restored to its pristine condition and safeguarded against future contamination.

The areas & materials that require treatment are:
 - affected framing wood
 - affected concrete floors
 - other general surface areas as required

Residual non-fungal staining may be present upon completion.

-- 4 - Post-Removal Clearance (Swab)

Post-remediation verification is conducted to ensure that the environment has been successfully remediated.

The final clearance inspection includes a visual inspection and an instant swab analysis.

This will be performed by the Project Supervisor upon completion of the remediation process.

-- Project Clearance Report

A written report following the remediation process, describing the outcome of the remediation work, any potential source issues, clearance grades, etc.

Additional recommendations will be made in this report to assist in preventing future fungal contamination.

-- Notes

- On-site inspection included upon acceptance to reconfirm the source and the extent

Report Info:

Observations

- The home was reportedly completed approximately two years ago, and the basement is unfinished.
- Basement relative humidity was reported to be above the recommended range.
- Visible discoloration was noted on the concrete floor and exposed wood framing studs.
- Ventilation within the basement appeared insufficient, potentially contributing to elevated humidity and conditions favourable to fungal growth.
- The basement is used for storage. Stored belongings restrict air circulation, particularly around concrete and framing, potentially contributing to localized moisture accumulation.
- The main HVAC system reportedly includes an integrated humidifier, which may contribute to elevated indoor humidity when operating.
- The sump pit was reportedly dry. However, this condition could prove that no intermittent groundwater intrusion or foundation seepage happened.

Suggestions and Recommendations

- Professional mold remediation is recommended to address the affected concrete and framing surfaces.
- Improve basement ventilation and air circulation.
- Operate a suitably sized dehumidifier to maintain relative humidity between 30% and 50%, both while ventilation improvements are pending and afterward as needed.
- Have the HVAC humidifier settings reviewed. Humidification should be reduced or disabled when indoor humidity is elevated, particularly during humid periods.
- Remove personal belongings from the affected area before remediation. Following remediation, organize storage to maintain airflow, and avoid placing items directly on the concrete floor.
